purpose: Dicloxacillin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, especially skin infections, bone infections, and infections caused by a type of bacteria called Staphylococcus (staph). It is specifically designed to fight staph bacteria that have become resistant to regular penicillin. Your doctor may prescribe it for things like infected wounds, cellulitis, or other soft tissue infections.
how_it_works: Dicloxacillin works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. It blocks the bacteria from building and repairing that protective wall, which causes the bacteria to fall apart and die. The special thing about this antibiotic is that it is built to resist the trick certain staph bacteria use to destroy regular penicillin, so it stays effective against those tougher germs.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, stomach upset, diarrhea, and vomiting. Some people may notice a mild skin rash. Taking it on an empty stomach helps it work better but may also increase stomach discomfort for some people.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop a severe rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or have trouble breathing, as these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction. Let your doctor know if you have ever had a penicillin or amoxicillin allergy before taking this medicine. If you develop severe or bloody diarrhea, contact your doctor, as this could be a sign of a serious bowel infection. Take the full course as prescribed, even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is fully treated.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth every 6 hours (four times a day). It should be taken on an empty stomach — at least 30 to 60 minutes before a meal or 2 hours after eating — so your body absorbs it properly. Always finish the entire prescription unless your doctor tells you to stop.
